issues.reason: The bundled `(Member $x new)` fires off exactly the `(PartOf $x sk_group_1)` premise a separate distribution rule would use, so every member still gets the property and nothing false or over-asserted enters the KB; and in a quotative ("…, he said") the whole clause including its description is what was reported, so "new" belongs inside the seal.

The genitive test is the part/component question, and the x86 version is a variant of Solaris rather than a component of it, so the rule selects the opaque `Possession`; `PartOf` asserts a component relation that does not hold.

The half that stands is that the plural convention pairs a group-level event with the per-member rule; it is overstated as a defect here, because the entire predication is sealed under `Theme` and nothing licenses one sealed term holding both an `(And …)` group event and an `(Implication …)` — the reviewer's own registered gap — while the omission puts nothing false into the KB.

gaps_confirmed: sealing a QUANTIFIED complement — a multi-atom attitude complement seals as `(And …)`, but nothing states how an `(Implication …)` produced by a definite-plural distributive complement is sealed under `Theme`
a post-posed quotative ", he said" with no "that" complementizer — the propositional-attitude section is written for a finite "that"-complement
new_gaps: free `$`-variables inside a sealed term — a seal is matched by rebuilding it with variables in the unknown slots, and nothing states how a sealed rule's own variables behave under that
repair_summary: Changed (PartOf sk_version_1 solaris) to (Possession sk_version_1 solaris) for "the x86 version of Solaris" (proof name updated to version_poss accordingly); every other atom kept verbatim.
notes: The antecedent-less "he", the narrow `Or` scoping, `Future` inside the consequent and the projected definite typings are all correct as parsed.
